title: enforce-resource-bound-service-roles-with-kms-failover-and-audit-sanitizer
author: Priya Menon
release_notes: Add resource-bound service roles with PDP-backed enforcement, KMS provider preference with automatic failover, and an audit sanitizer for PII redaction. Backwards compatible default policies retained; operators must opt into strict residency enforcement.
description: Context: Customers have asked for stronger guarantees that service principals cannot access cross-region encrypted keys or exfiltrate metadata when performing inference. This PR introduces resource-bound service roles (RBAC v2) that are evaluated against a Policy Decision Point (PDP) for residency and key-scope constraints, plus a KMS provider preference layer that silently fails over to approved providers when the preferred provider is unavailable. It also adds an audit sanitizer that strips or masks sensitive fields before shipping logs to multi-tenant analytics. Motivation: reduce blast radius of mis-scoped service accounts, make key selection resilient while preserving data residency controls, and prevent sensitive fields from leaking to downstream observability systems. Checklist: - [x] Implement PDP adapter and RBAC v2 policy hooks - [x] Add KMS provider preference and failover logic with operator-configurable allowlists - [x] Implement audit sanitizer with configurable redaction rules and signing - [x] E2E tests for policy enforcement paths and failover scenarios - [x] Migration script to populate resource-role bindings for existing service principals - [x] Documentation and operator guide updates Rollout plan: staged rollout behind feature flag (security.resource_bound_roles_v2). Start in canary, move to 10% region traffic, then global. When enabled, existing service principals are evaluated with a permissive migration mode for 72 hours before strict enforcement; operators will be notified of any rejected requests via a one-time report in the Console. Compatibility and operator impact: - Default behavior is backward compatible; strict residency enforcement is opt-in. - Operators must configure allowed KMS providers and region affinity for service accounts to avoid unexpected denials. - Audit sanitization is configurable per workspace; default rules mask common PII (email, credit_card_number, ssn). Security considerations: - PDP responses are cached for 5 minutes to avoid undue latency; cache TTL configurable per workspace. - Audit sanitizer runs before logs leave the control plane and signs the sanitized payload using the workspace CMK so downstream systems can verify provenance. - Added guardrails to ensure fallback KMS providers are only chosen if provider is approved by the workspace allowlist. Migration: includes a migration job that scans service accounts and adds a resource-role binding using existing tenant claims; operators must run the job post-deploy (instructions in docs). Backout: feature flag allows immediate disable of strict enforcement and failover behavior. Related work: ENG-1219 (RBAC v2 policy infra), SEC-87 (audit sanitization RFC).
